title: One Hundred and One Times
summary: The olas tamid offered at Sinai, the difference between an olah and a shelamim, and davening in place of korbanos. Then Bar Hei Hei's question: why learning something 101 times is so much greater than 100. Eliyahu's teaching that poverty suits Klal Yisrael like a red sash on a white horse, and the talmid chacham who strays like a bird from its nest.
key_ideas: Davening takes the place of the korbanos.
An olah goes entirely to Hashem; a shelamim is shared.
The one extra review, 101 times instead of 100, makes all the difference.
A talmid chacham who strays is like a bird that wanders from its nest.
